signals.evidence: In Baram, community leaders expressed lack of trust in politicians and the army, stating they told unrealistic stories and promised a quiet, secure border that did not materialize in reality.
In Abdon/Maaleh Yosef, there is concern that the army is not telling the truth.
In Liman/Matte Asher, message to IDF: 'Do not tell stories!'
In Baram, farmers report limited number of armored field protection booths (מיגוניות) relative to the scope of agricultural land.
In Baram, there is a shortage of protected spaces for educational and social activities; no suitable public space exists.
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, many residents lack individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); public shelters are not in optimal condition; some residents have shelters that are far from them.
In Abdon/Maaleh Yosef, not all elderly have individual safe rooms (ממ"דים); public shelters are far away; no possibility to reach shelters in time.
In Abdon/Maaleh Yosef, additional armored field protection booths (מיגוניות) are needed.
In Liman/Matte Asher, there are known protection gaps; all are in process of receiving solutions.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, there are protection gaps; elderly lack protection.
In Baram, informal activities began today; HFC volunteer corps (צח"י) training and volunteer reinforcement are underway.
In Abdon/Maaleh Yosef, informal activities are taking place; community coordinator is recruiting volunteers.
In Baram, there is concern about business collapse, specifically a pizzeria.
In Baram, there is a gap in educators; proposal to fill the gap with the help of reserve soldiers.
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, young people fled; those aged 40+ remained.
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, the narrative is to stay, though accompanied by difficulties.
In Abdon/Maaleh Yosef, residents are not leaving; community coordinator is recruiting volunteers; women's evening and activities for adults are held.

In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, community resilience is expressed in the willingness to enable what is possible without distraction; most of the population has returned to the settlement; there is a young functioning population; discourse of coping.
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, there is variation in reports about going out to work.
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, there is an increase in the number of calls to the 106 emergency hotline.
In Goren/Maaleh Yosef, elderly population faces distress; difficulty reaching safe rooms; sometimes injured.
In Abdon/Maaleh Yosef, expansion of activities for children is underway.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, there is basic youth activity.
In Liman/Matte Asher, there is a sense of loss of trust toward politicians and military personnel.
In Liman/Matte Asher, the central distress is lack of activities for children.
In Liman/Matte Asher, those who can afford it have individual safe rooms (ממ"דים).
In Liman/Matte Asher, there is difficulty protecting farmers' security.
In Liman/Matte Asher, HFC volunteer corps (צח"י) overall functions well.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, there is a community readiness unit (כיתת כוננות).
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, there is a sense of fatigue and erosion from the ongoing situation.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, community communication exists without evidence of toxic discourse.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, there is good relationship with the council and Home Front Command.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, HFC volunteer corps (צח"י) is not operating at full capacity.

In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, elderly and those with special needs feel there is no 'father and mother' - no entity within the community that has a complete picture of elderly and people with disabilities.
In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, there is a lack of precise mapping of the entire population because HFC is not operating at full capacity.

In Granot HaGalil/Maaleh Yosef, there is a lack of connection between welfare services and this population - elderly, urban residents, families with children with special needs, and other populations including women whose family members are in military service.
In Even Menahem/Maaleh Yosef, residents describe themselves as 'mentally ill people living here'; feeling of abandonment; 'we are the periphery of the periphery'.
In Baram, elderly population is receiving community support.
